title: Prototype-based Correlation Transfer for Sketch-based Image Retrieval with Incomplete Modality Streams

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Continual Learning Sketch-based Image Retrieval with Missing Data (CIM-SBIR) and proposes Prototype-based Correlation Transfer (PCT) to handle emerging classes and incomplete modalities, achieving strong performance while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
AI.motivation: Existing SBIR methods assume fixed data sizes and complete paired sketch-image modalities, which fails in real-world scenarios where classes grow continuously and some modalities are missing.
AI.method: The proposed PCT approach uses an adapter to fine-tune pre-trained models for continual learning, a graph attention-based scheme to capture inter-modal correlations for prototype-guided modality completion, and a consensual semantic constraint to preserve representation consistency across incremental sessions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across several datasets show that PCT performs effectively even when modalities are missing while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
AI.conclusion: Prototype-based Correlation Transfer provides an effective solution for continual sketch-based image retrieval under incomplete modality streams.

title: Shorter Chains via Macro Transitions: Constant-Factor Compression for Chain-of-Thought Counter Simulation

AI.tldr: The paper introduces two machine rewrites, order-k macro transitions and base-b counting, to compress chain-of-thought counter machine simulations by a constant factor while preserving exact language recognition and length generalization under moderate compression.
AI.motivation: Chain-of-thought constructions that make transformers Turing complete typically simulate one counter machine transition per token, making serial generation length proportional to runtime and creating a major computational cost.
AI.method: The authors propose order-k macro transitions that combine k reachable base transitions into one token (compressing length T to roughly T/k with vocabulary bounded by the base vocabulary raised to k) and base-b counting that processes b counter units per token during monotone decrement bursts, keeping both within the same CoT counter programming class.
AI.result: On six synthetic counter machine tasks including equal-count and three-sum arithmetic verification, transformers trained on compressed traces achieve the predicted trace-length reductions along with lower generation latency, fewer attention operations, and smaller key-value caches, while retaining length generalization under moderate compression and degrading in accuracy when compression becomes aggressive relative to the counting range.
AI.conclusion: Constant-factor compression via macro transitions and base-b counting reduces serial CoT generation cost without sacrificing exact recognition or length generalization within moderate compression regimes, though aggressive compression trades off accuracy and increases reachable vocabulary data scaling cost.

title: A Survey of Advancing Audio Super-Resolution and Bandwidth Extension from Discriminative to Generative Models

AI.tldr: This survey reviews audio super-resolution and bandwidth extension, tracing the shift from discriminative deterministic mapping models to generative modeling approaches and providing controlled empirical comparisons across representative methods.
AI.motivation: Audio super-resolution and bandwidth extension are inherently ill-posed because high-frequency content is missing, and early discriminative deep neural networks suffer from regression-to-the-mean effects and spectral over-smoothing.
AI.method: The survey categorizes and examines discriminative DNNs alongside generative approaches including autoregressive models, VAEs, GANs, diffusion and score-based models, flow-based methods, and Schrödinger bridges across representation domains, architectures, conditioning mechanisms, and quality-efficiency trade-offs, complemented by unified controlled experiments.
AI.result: Unified experiments on representative discriminative and generative methods provide controlled empirical evidence characterizing the trade-offs among reconstruction fidelity, perceptual quality, robustness, and computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: The survey establishes a structured taxonomy and practical roadmap for advancing audio super-resolution from deterministic point estimation to distribution-aware generative modeling, while highlighting emerging directions with LLMs and multimodal foundation models and open challenges in perceptual evaluation, deployment, and real-world generalization.

title: On Measuring Localization of Shortcuts in Deep Networks

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a counterfactual experiment design to measure layer-wise shortcut localization in deep networks and finds that shortcuts are distributed across the network rather than localized to specific layers.
AI.motivation: Shortcuts are spurious rules that perform well during training but fail to generalize, and designing principled mitigation methods requires understanding how shortcuts affect feature representations across layers.
AI.method: The authors introduce shortcut-inducing data skew during training and counterfactually compare models trained on clean versus skewed datasets using shortcut-learning localization metrics across CIFAR-10, Waterbirds, and CelebA with VGG, ResNet, DeiT, and ConvNeXt architectures.
AI.result: Localization metrics show that shortcut learning is distributed throughout the network rather than confined to specific layers, with earlier layers predominantly encoding spurious features and later layers predominantly forgetting core features predictive on clean data; moreover, the localization metrics are associated with the success of layer-wise training interventions.
AI.conclusion: Understanding that earlier layers encode spurious features while later layers forget core features explains layer-wise shortcut behavior and helps guide effective layer-wise training interventions.
